text: Adriano Mario Garsia (20 August 1928 – 6 October 2024[1]) was a Tunisian-born Italian American mathematician known for his work in analysis, combinatorics, representation theory, and algebraic geometry. He studied under Charles Loewner and authored research on representation theory, symmetric functions, and algebraic combinatorics. Together with Mark Haiman, he formulated the n! conjecture. The Garsia–Wachs algorithm for optimal binary search trees, which he developed with his student Michelle L. Wachs in 1977,[2] bears his name. Born to Italian Tunisians in Tunis on 20 August 1928, Garsia relocated to Rome in 1946.[3] As of 2023[update], he had 36 students and at least 200 descendants, according to the Mathematics Genealogy Project. He served on the faculty of the University of California, San Diego,[4] where he retired in 2013 after 57 years as a founding member of the Mathematics Department. At his 90th Birthday Conference in 2019, it was noted that he was the oldest principal investigator of a grant from the National Science Foundation in the United States.[5] In 2012, he was elected a fellow of the American Mathematical Society.[6]
